text:
priya.k: Bringing Ember-7B (int4) canary up in us-west-2. After ~120s we see steady mem growth per-host and a few worker OOMs. Starting logs below, any quick ideas?

priya.k: ```
[2026-03-10T14:21:12Z] serve: request id=abc123 model=ember-7b-int4 seq=1
[2026-03-10T14:23:35Z] mem: rss 6.2G -> 7.9G (120s)
[2026-03-10T14:23:36Z] kv_prefetch: queued 48 prefixes
[2026-03-10T14:23:36Z] oom: worker pid=42 killed by OOM
```

priya.k: Canary config: batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=512, prefetch_window=4, kv_prefetch=true

tom.b: ugh, looks like aggressive prefetch + high max_new_tokens. Ember's KV expansion combined with int4's allocation fragmentation can do that.

jane.l: +1. Try dropping prefetch_window to 1 and max_new_tokens to 256 for the canary. Also enable kv_trim_idle=30s to free stale KV shards.

priya.k: will try. before i change, is there a safe way to repro locally with smaller requests?

sanjay: you can run the repro harness with shorter prompts but loop to simulate long generation: `./tools/loadgen --model ember-7b-int4 --max-new 512 --concurrency 6 --iterations 200`

maya: also add `--kv-report` to that harness to print per-step KV allocations, helps spot leaks.

priya.k: switched canary to prefetch_window=1, max_new_tokens=256, kv_trim_idle=30s. patch below:

priya.k: ```yaml
model: ember-7b-int4
batch_size: 4
max_new_tokens: 256
prefetch_window: 1
kv_prefetch: true
kv_trim_idle: 30s
```

infra-bot: deploy started: canary ember-7b-int4 -> pool-ember-canary-2 (uid: d6f8)

priya.k: after ~10m the mem growth flattened. saw one soft OOM that recovered with fallback to int8.

tom.b: good sign. can you paste the kv-report from the harness? curious about growth shape.

priya.k: ```
KV_REPORT: step=1 active=12kB total_alloc=12kB
KV_REPORT: step=50 active=1.1MB total_alloc=1.2MB
KV_REPORT: step=120 active=5.8MB total_alloc=6.0MB
KV_REPORT: step=180 active=5.9MB total_alloc=6.0MB
```

jane.l: that pattern (rapid ramp then plateau) is classic KV warmup + fragmentation. trimming + smaller max_new avoided further reservations. two followups: 1) add a small MV threshold so very small prefixes aren't prefetched, 2) we should add an Ember-specific quant fallback rule in runtime to drop to int8 after X soft OOMs.

sanjay: i'll open a follow-up PR for runtime fallback + a telemetry tag for 'kv_warmup' so ops can detect this.

maya: also worth adding a default max_new_tokens override in the model catalog for ember-7b-int4 -> 256 (with note). reduce surprise for self-serve users.

priya.k: opened canary followup issue: https://redwood.internal/rd/issue/ML-4032 (notes + repro steps). tagging @oncall to watch for regressions.

infra-bot: alert muted for 1h for pool-ember-canary-2 (reason: canary adjustments)

tom.b: quick doc blurb we can add to onboarding checklist: "For int4 canaries, prefer prefetch_window <=1 and conservative max_new_tokens (<=256) until KV warmup profiles are observed."

jane.l: i'll add the doc. thanks all. :tada:
